state.instructions: Classify the storage alternatives using only the facts provided here. Do not research, infer an implemented runtime, or regard a recommendation as validation.
state.facts: canlang targets economical adoption with compact, reliable SaaS declarations. First-class Cloudflare services are a user requirement, whereas the CanCheck line splitting D1 configuration/history from DO heartbeat authority was introduced in its draft and was not a user demand. Current ownership is D1 for Check/Transition and for Employee/Location. DESIGN confines each mutation to one authority, requires a moved root group to share its DO, and disallows pretending mutable cross-owner queries are atomic. The shown can_work implementation determines genuine location access; its Employee data is absent from the trusted role/membership snapshot. The proposed D1 fence commits all writes in one batch. Timers already have a D1 dispatcher path and a DO-alarm path. Neither path has been implemented or benchmarked. Completion still needs durable receipt responses, initial and repeated missed heartbeats, grace periods, recovery, pause/resume, timer revisions, separate notification outcomes, retention, and trusted technical provisioning with no product UI/MCP surface. Developer writes must participate in normal owner fencing. These behaviors are expressible with D1 authority; D1 contention remains unknown.

storage.instructions: Which revision best balances adoption and small language surface with unchanged access restrictions, truthful atomicity and honest performance limits?

criteria.d1: Retain D1 authority for the check root and its health/alert children, retain can_work, and correct the provisional split-owner requirement. Use the existing shared timer dispatcher. It adds no authorization contract, but throughput under the whole-database fence and delayed dispatch still require a prototype.
criteria.do_snapshot: Choose a DO for each complete check group and add a newly specified D1 Employee-grant admission snapshot. Per-check ordering and alarms become local, at the cost of extra language/runtime authorization work and a revocation interval that is not atomic with the Employee row.
criteria.defer: Decline to resolve placement now, explicitly keeping the authorization/split-owner mismatch open. This reserves judgment until implementation evidence arrives, but prevents closing a behavior that D1 can already describe and leaves contradictory draft text intact.
